sources.entry: This list is made by the team behind e2b. E2b is building AWS for AI agents. We help developers to deploy, test, and monitor AI agents. E2b is agnostic to your tech stack and aims to work with any tooling for building AI agents.

summary.one_liner: E2B is open-source infrastructure for running AI-generated code in secure, isolated cloud sandboxes, controlled through JavaScript and Python SDKs.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides the E2B SDKs for starting and controlling cloud sandboxes. The base SDK (npm i e2b / pip install e2b) lets you create a sandbox and run shell commands in it, returning stdout. A separate Code Interpreter SDK (@e2b/code-interpreter / e2b-code-interpreter) adds runCode()/run_code() for executing code and getting its output. A Desktop SDK (@e2b/desktop / e2b-desktop) adds mouse, keyboard, screenshot, application launch, and desktop streaming APIs for computer-use agents. The README also points to documentation and a cookbook of examples with different LLMs and AI frameworks. For self-hosting, it describes deploying the E2B runtime on your own infrastructure using Terraform, on AWS, GCP, Azure, or a general Linux machine via Embed.
use_cases: run AI-generated code safely in isolated sandboxes
execute shell commands inside a cloud sandbox from code
computer-use agents that control a virtual desktop
self-host sandbox infrastructure on your own cloud
how_to_run: npm i e2b (JavaScript/TypeScript) or pip install e2b (Python)
Sign up for E2B and get an API key
Create a sandbox with Sandbox.create() and run commands with sandbox.commands.run()
Optional: npm i @e2b/code-interpreter or pip install e2b-code-interpreter for runCode()/run_code()
Optional: npm i @e2b/desktop or pip install e2b-desktop for desktop control; self-hosting is covered by the embed deployment guide
notable: Separate SDK packages for commands, code interpreter, and desktop control
Computer-use desktop API with screenshots and mouse/keyboard control
Self-hosting via Terraform on AWS, GCP, Azure, or any Linux machine
Python SDK supports context-manager use (with Sandbox.create())
caveats: Cloud use requires signing up for an E2B account and API key
Self-hosting requires setting up infrastructure via Terraform and the embed deployment guide
The README does not state pricing or license terms
